Maximum-of-L sensitivity bound (Rosenbaum 2012, procedure 6)

Source: R/rosenbaum-pairs.R
riposte_pairs_bound.Rd

Given L score columns H for the same matched pairs, computes each statistic T_l = sum B_i H[i, l], its standardized worst-case deviate at sensitivity gamma, and the upper bound on the one-sided p-value of their maximum from the multivariate normal orthant probability implied by crossprod(H).

Usage

riposte_pairs_bound(y, H, gamma = 1, algorithm = NULL)

Arguments

y

matched-pair differences.

H

numeric matrix, one row per pair, one column per statistic (2 <= L).

gamma

sensitivity parameter, >= 1.

algorithm

an mvtnorm algorithm object. Default: mvtnorm::Miwa() for L <= 5 (what testtwice uses), else mvtnorm::GenzBretz() (Miwa is exponentially slow in L; GenzBretz is Monte Carlo, so set a seed).

Value

a list with p.value, deviates, and cor.

Details

This is a normal approximation (as in the paper and in testtwice::tt()). riposte_pairs_perm_test() computes the same bound from the distribution of the signs instead, which is what riposte_test() does unless engine = "asymptotic".

References

Rosenbaum, P. R. (2012) Testing one hypothesis twice in observational studies. Biometrika 99(4), 763-774. See also the CRAN package testtwice.
